question: where does the quran say Allah is closer to us than our jugular vein?
gold_answer: This is Surah Qaf 50:16: Allah says He created man, knows what his soul whispers to him, and is nearer to him than his jugular vein.
notes: Scholars commonly explain the nearness as nearness by knowledge (and His angels); the verse itself mentions knowing what the soul whispers.

question: Is there an ayah where Allah says He is near and answers whoever calls Him?
gold_answer: Yes, Al-Baqarah 2:186: when My servants ask about Me, I am near; I answer the call of the caller when he calls on Me, so let them respond to Me and believe in Me. Ghafir 40:60 similarly says 'Call on Me, I will respond to you.'

question: the verse that says Allah won't change a people's situation until they change themselves, where is it?
gold_answer: Ar-Ra'd 13:11: Allah does not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves. The same verse mentions guardian angels in front of and behind each person, by Allah's command.
must_not: attributing it to Surah Al-Anfal only (8:53 has a similar meaning)
notes: 8:53 carries a similar idea about blessings; 13:11 is the commonly quoted verse.

question: Which ayah promises that the Quran will be protected from change?
gold_answer: Al-Hijr 15:9: 'Indeed, We sent down the Reminder (the Quran), and indeed We are its guardian.' Allah Himself guarantees its preservation.

question: verse calling the Prophet a mercy to all the worlds
gold_answer: Al-Anbiya 21:107: 'We have not sent you except as a mercy to the worlds.'

question: where in the Quran is Muhammad ﷺ called the last prophet / seal of prophets?
gold_answer: Al-Ahzab 33:40: Muhammad is not the father of any of your men, but he is the Messenger of Allah and the Seal (Khatam) of the Prophets.
notes: Verse is also cited for the context of Zayd ibn Haritha (adoption); finality of prophethood is the main point here.

question: "remember me and I will remember you" which surah is that from
gold_answer: Al-Baqarah 2:152: 'So remember Me; I will remember you. Be grateful to Me and do not deny Me.'

question: where's the ayah about Allah being the light of the heavens and earth with the lamp and niche example
gold_answer: This is the Verse of Light, An-Nur 24:35: Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth; His light is likened to a niche containing a lamp in a glass like a shining star, lit from a blessed olive tree neither of the east nor west - light upon light.

question: Allah says if you are grateful I will give you more - where is that?
gold_answer: Ibrahim 14:7: your Lord proclaimed, 'If you are grateful, I will surely increase you; but if you are ungrateful, My punishment is severe.'

question: whoever fears Allah, He makes a way out for him and provides from where he never expected. verse number?
gold_answer: At-Talaq 65:2-3: whoever is mindful of Allah, He will make a way out for him and provide for him from where he does not expect; and whoever relies on Allah, He is sufficient for him.
must_mention: provide from where he does not expect
notes: The promise sits at the end of 65:2 and continues into 65:3, inside passages on divorce.

question: which verse tells us to send salawat on the Prophet?
gold_answer: Al-Ahzab 33:56: Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet; O you who believe, send blessings upon him and greet him with peace.

question: Quran verse about responding to bad treatment with good so your enemy becomes like a close friend
gold_answer: Fussilat 41:34: good and evil are not equal; repel evil with what is better, and the one between whom and you there was enmity will become like a devoted friend.
must_mention: repel evil with what is better
notes: 23:96 has a shorter similar command.

question: the ayah about the amanah (trust) that the heavens and mountains refused but man accepted?
gold_answer: Al-Ahzab 33:72: Allah offered the trust to the heavens, the earth and the mountains; they declined it and feared it, but man took it on - indeed he was unjust and ignorant.

question: I remember a verse saying if the Quran was sent on a mountain it would crumble from fear of Allah. where?
gold_answer: Al-Hashr 59:21: if We had sent down this Quran upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled and split apart from fear of Allah; such examples are given so people may reflect.

question: which verse has Ibrahim asking Allah to show him how He brings the dead to life, with the birds?
gold_answer: Al-Baqarah 2:260: Ibrahim asked to be shown how Allah gives life to the dead, saying it was so his heart would be reassured; he was told to take four birds, put parts of them on hills and call them, and they came to him in haste.

question: what is surah al asr about?
gold_answer: Surah Al-'Asr (103) swears by time and declares that mankind is in loss, except those who believe, do righteous deeds, and urge one another to the truth and to patience.

question: What are we seeking protection from in Surah al-Falaq?
gold_answer: Surah Al-Falaq (113) seeks refuge in the Lord of the daybreak from the evil of what He created, the darkness when it settles, those who blow on knots (witchcraft), and the envier when he envies.
notes: An-Nas (114) is the companion surah seeking refuge from the whisperer.

question: what does surah kafirun say
gold_answer: Surah Al-Kafirun (109) tells the Prophet to say to the disbelievers that he does not worship what they worship and they do not worship what he worships, ending with 'For you is your religion, and for me is mine.'
must_mention: I do not worship what you worship
must_not: presenting 109:6 as saying all religions are equally true

question: what advice did Luqman give his son in the Quran?
gold_answer: In Surah Luqman 31:13-19 he tells his son not to associate partners with Allah (shirk is a great wrong), that Allah brings forth even a mustard seed's weight of deeds, to establish prayer, enjoin good and forbid evil, be patient, not turn his cheek in arrogance or walk proudly, and to be moderate in pace and lower his voice. Verses 14-15 in between command kindness to parents.

question: what qualities of successful believers are listed at the start of surah muminun?
gold_answer: Al-Mu'minun 23:1-11: the successful believers are humble in prayer, turn away from vain talk, pay zakah, guard their chastity (except with spouses), keep their trusts and promises, and guard their prayers; they will inherit Firdaws.

question: Who are 'ibad ar-rahman' and what are they like?
gold_answer: Al-Furqan 25:63 onwards describes the servants of the Most Merciful: they walk humbly and answer the ignorant with 'peace', spend the night in prostration and standing, ask to be saved from Hell, spend neither wastefully nor stingily, avoid shirk, unjust killing and zina, do not witness falsehood, and pray for righteous spouses and children.

question: surah al maun - what kind of person is it criticizing
gold_answer: Surah Al-Ma'un (107) describes the one who denies the Recompense: he repels the orphan and does not encourage feeding the poor; and woe to those who pray but are heedless of their prayer, who show off, and who withhold small acts of help.

question: what happened in surah al fil
gold_answer: Surah Al-Fil (105) recalls how Allah dealt with the companions of the elephant: He foiled their plan and sent flocks of birds pelting them with stones of baked clay, leaving them like chewed-up straw.
notes: The surah does not name Abraha or the Ka'bah; those details come from tafsir/seerah works (e.g. Ibn Kathir).

question: How many people of the cave were there? Quran gives the number right?
gold_answer: No definite number is given. Al-Kahf 18:22 reports people saying three with their dog, five with their dog, or seven with their dog - 'guessing at the unseen' - and tells the Prophet to say 'My Lord knows best their number; none knows them except a few,' and not to argue about them.
must_not: stating a definite number as Quranic fact
notes: Some mufassirun (e.g. Ibn Abbas via tafsir works) lean to seven because the third view is not called guessing; that comes from tafsir books, not the verse text.

question: what was Yusuf's dream in the Quran?
gold_answer: Yusuf 12:4: he told his father he saw eleven stars, the sun and the moon prostrating to him. His father warned him not to tell his brothers lest they plot against him (12:5), and the dream was fulfilled when his parents and brothers bowed before him in Egypt (12:100).

question: explain the story of Musa and Khidr - why did Khidr do those strange things
gold_answer: In Al-Kahf 18:60-82 Musa follows a servant whom Allah gave knowledge (18:65). He damaged a boat, killed a boy, and rebuilt a wall without pay. He then explained: the boat belonged to poor people and a king was seizing every sound ship; the boy's believing parents would have been burdened by his rebellion and disbelief; and the wall hid the treasure of two orphans whose father was righteous - all done by Allah's command, not his own.
notes: The name Khidr comes from hadith (e.g. Bukhari's Musa-Khidr narrations), not the Quran text; bukhari ref not verified here so not cited.

question: story of Adam's two sons in the quran
gold_answer: Al-Ma'idah 5:27-31: both sons offered a sacrifice; one was accepted and the other not. The rejected one threatened to kill his brother, who replied that Allah accepts only from the God-fearing and he would not raise his hand to kill him. He killed him anyway, then Allah sent a raven digging the ground to show him how to bury his brother, and he became regretful.
must_not: Quran naming them Habil and Qabil (names are from later tradition)

question: in fatiha who are 'those who earned anger' and 'those astray'?
gold_answer: Al-Fatihah 1:7 asks for the path of those Allah favoured, not of those who earned His anger nor those who went astray. In a hadith from Adi ibn Hatim the Prophet ﷺ said the Jews are those Allah is angry with and the Christians are those who strayed (Tirmidhi 2954).
notes: Tirmidhi 2954 graded Sahih by Shakir, Hasan by Albani. Ibn Kathir notes the general lesson: anger for those who knew and did not act, misguidance for those who acted without knowledge.

question: 6:82 says believers who don't mix belief with zulm are safe - but everyone does some wrong?
gold_answer: The Companions asked exactly this when 6:82 was revealed. The Prophet ﷺ explained that the 'wrong' (zulm) meant is shirk, citing Luqman's words 'associating partners with Allah is a great wrong' (31:13).
notes: Bukhari 32 labels the verse '6:83' in its English; the verse is 6:82 in standard numbering.

question: What are muhkam and mutashabih verses?
gold_answer: Al 'Imran 3:7 says the Book has clear, decisive verses (muhkam) which are its foundation, and others that are ambiguous (mutashabih). Those with deviation in their hearts chase the ambiguous ones seeking fitnah and their hidden meaning, while the firmly grounded say 'we believe in it, all is from our Lord.' The Prophet ﷺ said: when you see those who follow the ambiguous verses, they are the ones Allah named, so beware of them.
must_mention: beware of those who follow the ambiguous
notes: Whether the 'firmly grounded' also know the ta'wil depends on where one pauses in recitation - a known difference among mufassirun; a tafsir book adds detail.

question: fasting ayah says eat until the white thread is distinct from the black thread - what thread?
gold_answer: In 2:187 the threads are not literal. Adi ibn Hatim put a white and a black string under his pillow and could not tell them apart; the Prophet ﷺ told him it means the darkness of the night and the whiteness of dawn.

question: how did christians and jews 'take their rabbis as lords' if they didn't worship them?
gold_answer: At-Tawbah 9:31 says they took their rabbis and monks as lords besides Allah. When Adi ibn Hatim heard it, the Prophet ﷺ explained they did not worship them, but when the scholars made something lawful they took it as lawful and when they forbade something they took it as forbidden - obeying them in making halal and haram.
must_mention: obeying them in halal and haram
notes: Tirmidhi 3095 graded Hasan by Shakir and Albani, Da'if by Zubair Ali Zai - mention grading caveat.

question: Quran says 'no sin' to go between Safa and Marwa - does that mean sa'i is optional?
gold_answer: Urwa understood 2:158 that way and Aisha corrected him: had it meant optional it would say 'no sin if he does not go between them.' She explained it was revealed because the Ansar, who used to assume ihram for the idol Manat, felt uneasy about going between Safa and Marwa, so Allah said there is no sin in it. The verse calls them symbols of Allah.
notes: The legal status of sa'i (rukn vs wajib) differs among madhhabs; this item is about the verse's wording and context, not the ruling.

question: Who was the blind man in surah abasa?
gold_answer: Surah 'Abasa (80:1-3) was revealed about Ibn Umm Maktum, a blind man who came asking the Prophet ﷺ for guidance while he was busy with a leading man of the idolaters; the Prophet turned away from him and the verses were revealed (Tirmidhi 3331, from Aisha).

question: what is al kawthar exactly
gold_answer: In Surah 108 Allah says He gave the Prophet al-Kawthar. The Prophet ﷺ described it as a river in Paradise he was shown, with banks of tents of hollow pearl (Tirmidhi 3359). Ibn Abbas explained it as the abundant good Allah gave him, and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said the river in Paradise is part of that good (Bukhari 4966).

question: surah nasr is about victory, why did ibn abbas say it was about the prophet's death?
gold_answer: When Umar asked the senior Companions about 110:1, they said it was about future conquests; Ibn Abbas said it signalled the end of the Prophet's ﷺ life - when victory and the conquest come and people enter Islam in crowds, that is the sign his death is near, so glorify and seek forgiveness. Umar agreed with him.
must_mention: sign the Prophet's death was near

question: what does 'ummatan wasatan' mean in 2:143?
gold_answer: 2:143 calls the Muslims a 'wasat' nation so they may be witnesses over mankind and the Messenger a witness over them. The Prophet ﷺ explained wasat means just, and described the Day of Judgement when Nuh's people deny he warned them and Muhammad and his ummah testify that he did.

question: what are the pillars of iman?
gold_answer: In the hadith of Jibril the Prophet ﷺ said iman is to believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and to believe in the divine decree (qadar), its good and its evil (Muslim, from Umar). The Quran lists belief in Allah, His angels, books, messengers and the Last Day (2:285, 4:136).
notes: muslim:93 is Abd al-Baqi 8a. Bukhari 50 (Abu Huraira) gives a shorter list without qadar.

question: are any angels named in the quran?
gold_answer: Yes. Jibril (Gabriel) and Mika'il (Michael) are named in 2:98. Malik, the keeper of Hell, is addressed by the people of the Fire in 43:77, and Harut and Marut are named in 2:102.
notes: Pickthall renders 43:77's 'Ya Malik' as 'O master'; Arabic has the name Malik.

question: do angels write down everything we do?
gold_answer: Yes. Qaf 50:17-18 describes two receivers seated on the right and the left, and not a word is uttered without an observer ready to record it. Al-Infitar 82:10-12 says there are guardians over you, noble recorders, who know what you do.

question: Which books did Allah reveal before the quran?
gold_answer: The Quran names the Tawrah (Torah) and the Injil (Gospel) (3:3), the Zabur (Psalms) given to Dawud (4:163), and the scrolls (suhuf) of Ibrahim and Musa (87:18-19). The Quran confirms what came before it.
must_not: claiming the current Bible is identical to the revealed Injil

question: do muslims believe jesus was crucified?
gold_answer: No. An-Nisa 4:157-158 says they did not kill him nor crucify him, but it was made to appear so to them; rather Allah raised him up to Himself.

question: Is everything that happens already written by Allah?
gold_answer: Yes. Al-Hadid 57:22 says no calamity strikes on earth or in yourselves except that it is in a Book before Allah brings it into being, and Al-Qamar 54:49 says Allah created everything by measure. The Prophet ﷺ told Ibn Abbas that if all creation gathered to benefit or harm you, they could only do what Allah had written - the pens are lifted and the pages dry (Tirmidhi 2516).

question: can anyone intercede for someone on judgment day?
gold_answer: Only with Allah's permission. Ta-Ha 20:109 says on that Day no intercession benefits except of one whom the Most Merciful permits and whose word He approves; Saba 34:23 likewise says intercession avails only for whom He permits.
notes: Details of the Prophet's intercession come from long hadith (e.g. Bukhari's shafa'a narrations), not cited here.

question: will believers actually see Allah in jannah?
gold_answer: Yes, according to the Quran and authentic hadith. Al-Qiyamah 75:22-23 says on that Day some faces will be radiant, looking at their Lord. The Prophet ﷺ, looking at the full moon, said 'You will see your Lord as you see this moon, with no trouble in seeing Him' (Bukhari).
notes: Ahl al-Sunnah affirm the vision; Mu'tazila denied it - that history is from aqeedah books.

question: who knows when the day of judgement will be?
gold_answer: Only Allah. Luqman 31:34 says with Allah alone is knowledge of the Hour, and He sends rain and knows what is in the wombs; no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow or in what land it will die. Al-An'am 6:59 says the keys of the unseen are with Him; none knows them but He.
must_not: giving a date for the Day of Judgement

question: was shaytan an angel? what's he made of
gold_answer: No. Al-Kahf 18:50 says Iblis was of the jinn and disobeyed his Lord's command when the angels prostrated to Adam. The jinn were created from smokeless fire (55:15; 15:27), while man was created from clay (55:14).
notes: The hadith that angels were created from light is in Sahih Muslim but was not located/verified in this corpus pass, so not cited.

question: is punishment of the grave in the quran or only hadith?
gold_answer: Both indicate it. Ghafir 40:46 says Pharaoh's people are exposed to the Fire morning and evening, and then on the Day the Hour is established they enter the severest punishment - showing punishment before Resurrection. The Prophet ﷺ confirmed to Aisha 'Yes, there is punishment in the grave' and sought refuge from it in every prayer (Bukhari 1372).
must_mention: yes, there is punishment in the grave

question: how many prophets did Allah send? are they all named in the quran?
gold_answer: The Quran does not give a total. It says some messengers' stories were told to the Prophet and some were not (40:78; 4:164). It names a number of them, e.g. Nuh, Ibrahim, Isma'il, Ishaq, Ya'qub, 'Isa, Ayyub, Yunus, Harun, Sulayman and Dawud in 4:163.
notes: Figures like 124,000 prophets come from hadith in Musnad Ahmad etc. (not in this corpus); the commonly cited count of 25 named in the Quran is from scholars' tallies.

question: how will deeds be weighed on the day of judgement?
gold_answer: Allah will set up just scales (mizan) on the Day of Resurrection so no soul is wronged, even a mustard seed's weight is brought (21:47). Whoever's scales are heavy will have a pleasing life, and whoever's are light, his abode is the Abyss (101:6-9).

question: what dua did the prophet make the most?
gold_answer: Anas reported the Prophet's ﷺ most frequent supplication was: 'O Allah, our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire' (Bukhari 6389) - the dua from Al-Baqarah 2:201.

question: dua of yunus in the whale?
gold_answer: 'La ilaha illa anta, subhanaka, inni kuntu minaz-zalimin' - there is no god but You, glory be to You, I was among the wrongdoers (21:87). Allah answered him and saved him (21:88), and the Prophet ﷺ said no Muslim supplicates with it for anything except that Allah responds (Tirmidhi 3505).

question: what's sayyidul istighfar and why is it special
gold_answer: It is the best form of seeking forgiveness: 'Allahumma anta Rabbi la ilaha illa anta, khalaqtani wa ana 'abduka ... faghfir li fa innahu la yaghfirudh-dhunuba illa anta.' The Prophet ﷺ said whoever says it in the day with firm faith and dies before evening, or at night and dies before morning, will be of the people of Paradise (Bukhari 6306).

question: What do muslims say when someone dies or something bad happens?
gold_answer: 'Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un' - we belong to Allah and to Him we return (2:156). The Prophet ﷺ taught adding 'O Allah, reward me in my affliction and replace it with something better', and Allah gives something better; Umm Salama said it and was given the Prophet ﷺ as husband after Abu Salama (Muslim).
must_mention: inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un
notes: muslim:2126 = Abd al-Baqi 918a.

question: which two phrases are light on the tongue but heavy on the scale?
gold_answer: 'SubhanAllahi wa bihamdihi' and 'SubhanAllahil-'Azim'. The Prophet ﷺ said these are easy on the tongue, heavy in the balance and beloved to the Most Merciful (Bukhari 6406).

question: which Quran verse mentions abu bakr in the cave during hijrah
gold_answer: At-Tawbah 9:40 refers to the Prophet ﷺ as 'the second of two' in the cave, telling his companion 'Do not grieve, Allah is with us.' Abu Bakr narrated he said 'if one of them looked under his feet he would see us', and the Prophet replied 'What do you think of two whose third is Allah?' (Bukhari 3653).
notes: 9:40 does not name Abu Bakr; the identification comes from the hadith.

question: what happened right after the first revelation in cave hira?
gold_answer: After the angel squeezed him and taught him 'Read in the name of your Lord', the Prophet ﷺ returned to Khadija with his heart trembling, saying 'Cover me!' She reassured him Allah would never disgrace him because he kept family ties and helped the poor and guests, then took him to her cousin Waraqa ibn Nawfal, who said this was the same angel sent to Musa (Bukhari 3).

question: Did angels fight at the battle of Badr? how many muslims were there
gold_answer: The Quran says Allah gave victory at Badr when the Muslims were weak (3:123) and answered their call for help with a thousand angels following one another (8:9), inspiring the angels to make the believers firm (8:12). The Companions said the people of Badr were a little over 310, the number of Talut's men who crossed the river (Bukhari 3957).
notes: 313/314 commonly quoted in seerah books; the hadith says 'over three hundred and ten'.

question: what was bay'at ar-ridwan and how many companions took it?
gold_answer: It was the pledge of allegiance the Companions gave the Prophet ﷺ under the tree at al-Hudaybiyah; Allah says He was pleased with the believers when they pledged under the tree and sent tranquillity on them (48:18). Al-Bara' said they were 1,400 that day and considered this pledge the real 'victory' of 48:1 (Bukhari 4150).
notes: Bukhari 4155 gives 1300 from Ibn Abi Awfa; 1400 is the more widely reported number.

question: why did the muslims lose at uhud
gold_answer: The Prophet ﷺ placed fifty archers under Abdullah ibn Jubayr and ordered them not to leave their position even if they saw the Muslims winning. When the enemy fled, most left to collect booty, and the Muslims were then routed (Bukhari 3039). The Quran says in 3:152 that their courage failed, they disputed the order and disobeyed after Allah had shown them what they loved - some wanted this world - yet Allah forgave them.
